thread:
Ravi: Quick alert: Thalassa-11B int4 onboarding regression on summarization evals. avg Rouge-L fell 35.8 -> 30.7 across newsbench. Repro on nf4 profile.
Lina: Oof. Which conversion path? hf->redwood or pb->redwood?
Ravi: hf->redwood via converter v0.9.3. Converter log looked okay but runtime shows some rotary mismatch warnings.
Zoe: Any runtime warnings? paste them.
Ravi: snippet:
```
[WARN] rotary_meta_mismatch: checkpoint contains 'rotary_alpha_scale' but runtime expects 'rotary_phase_scale' -> defaulting to 1.0
[WARN] kv_cache_offset: observed=256 expected=255
```
Marco: That kv offset + rotary defaulting is suspicious. Even a 1-token slip can desync KV reuse.
Lina: Did you test with prefix cache disabled?
Ravi: yes. With --prefix-cache=false Rouge-L moves from 30.7 -> 32.1. With explicit rotary_phase_scale taken from fp16 header (1.0172) it goes to 33.9. Both together 34.8, close but not identical.
Zoe: So three factors: rotary key name mismatch, token id mapping, and maybe unicode normalization difference. Any tokenmap diffs?
Ravi: Ran tokenmap diff vs fp16 map. Differences concentrated around first 512 tokens and a handful of combining diacritics. Output summary: 213 diffs in first 512, 19 diffs > 1000.
Lina: That screams merge-table reordering or NFKD vs NFKC change during conversion. Which normalizer does the converter apply?
Ravi: Converter used "lexnorm: normalize_nfkd=true" by default. The original tokenizer used nfkc. I think we silently changed normalization.
Marco: Yikes. If converter changed normalization, token boundaries change -> different token ids for same text -> KV alignment break.
Zoe: Quick mitigation: add a conversion flag --preserve-normalization and an assertion in the runtime that checkpoint.normalization == tokenizer.normalization.
Ravi: Filed an issue: https://git.internal/converter/issue/502 and started a branch to add --preserve-normalization.
ci-bot: Job queued: thalassa-int4-bisect (id: 7124). Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/7124/logs
Lina: For the bisect, include these modes: (A) load int4 checkpoint but override rotary_phase_scale with fp16 value; (B) run int4 tokenizer using fp16.tokenmap; (C) run with both fixes. Collect top-50 divergent tokens and KV snapshots for first 6 steps.
Ravi: Command I'm running now:
```bash
python -m eval.run \
  --model thalassa-11b-int4-nf4 \
  --tokenizer thalassa-vocab.json \
  --batch 12 \
  --prefix-cache true \
  --rotary-phase-scale 1.0172 \
  --quant-profile nf4 \
  --dump-kv 6 \
  --dump-attn 2
```
Zoe: Also capture tokenization side-by-side for each eval prompt: both token id arrays and detokenized text. It helps spot tiny invisible differences (zero-width joiner etc).
Ravi: Will do. Quick note: int4 kernel selection sometimes applies an internal scale tweak for numeric stability. If runtime picks a different microkernel due to key mismatch, that could change logits slightly.
Marco: Good point. We should log the chosen kernel variant in init: e.g., `selected_kernel=rotary_int4_stable_v2` vs `rotary_fp16_standard`. Add that to hotfix.
Lina: I've started a runtime PR to: 1) fail loudly if expected rotary keys missing 2) emit selected_kernel and rotary metadata in init log 3) add a toggle to force kernel variant.
ci-bot: Job 7124 started on node a100-gpu-12. Artifacts will be at https://ci.internal/artifacts/7124/

Zoe: If converter changed normalization, switching it back might restore token ids but we also need to ensure merge-table ordering reproducibility. Add a test that roundtrips hf tokenizer -> converter -> loader and checks id equality for 5k real-world sentences.
Ravi: Added a quick test in tools/tokenmap_roundtrip.sh. Initial run shows 98.6% exact id agreement across 5k sentences; failures concentrated on punctuation + combining marks.
Marco: For immediate customer safety, gate the int4 profile: mark as experimental and default to off in Dedicated until conversion fix + runtime checks land.
Lina: I'll prepare a short mitigation note for support and document the feature flag (FF_INT4_THALASSA).
Ravi: job 7124 results: when forcing fp16 rotary_phase + fp16 tokenmap we recover to 35.6 Rouge-L (within 0.2 of baseline). Forcing only rotary gives 33.9; only tokenmap gives 34.2. So it's additive. Dumps: https://ci.internal/artifacts/7124/dumps.tar.gz
Zoe: Nice bisect. That confirms two orthogonal defects: normalization->token id drift and rotary key mismatch -> kernel selection.
Marco: Next steps: Sam (converter) to add preserve-normalization + stable merge-table ordering; Lina (runtime) to fail loud on missing rotary metadata + log kernel; Ravi (eval) to add tokenmap roundtrip test to onboarding checklist. Owners?
Ravi: I'll own eval + mitigation note. Lina owns runtime PR. Marco will coordinate gating and support comms.
ci-bot: Created ticket infra/task/941: "Thalassa int4 onboarding: converter + runtime fixes"
Lina: Will open runtime PR within 2 hours.
Ravi: Thanks team. Will post a minimal repro (prompt, token ids, kv snapshots) after I upload dumps. Expect ~30m.
